Since similar functionality already exists in BezierTrackEditor, I assume it would be better to unify the terms to Auto Tangent.
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/64647

> Since similar functionality already exists in BezierTrackEditor, I assume it would be better to unify the terms to Auto Tangent. #64647

When you say unify the terms, do you mean just change the nomenclature from 'Smooth Points' to 'Auto Tangent' or something similar?  @TokageItLab
Path3D is a pretty good node to use for reference to build some shapes, I could see this being useful to quickly get curves added to the entire path when you know you need them.

Implemented the equivalent functionality for Path2D also, with the caveat that currently the 'closed' curves in Path3D behave a bit differently to Path3D so I might tweak the algorithm to handle the way Path2D closed curves work

> When you say unify the terms, do you mean just change the nomenclature from 'Smooth Points' to 'Auto Tangent' or something similar? @TokageItLab

Exactly.

However, since what you're implementing isn't a toggle function but rather an option that wouldn't be triggered very frequently, I believe it should be called from the "Options" dropdown menu.

> However, since what you're implementing isn't a toggle function but rather an option that wouldn't be triggered very frequently, I believe it should be called from the "Options" dropdown menu.

It's not a toggle function but it's a button that can be pressed multiple times once you've modified the curve, so I think it would be nice to not have it hidden away behind options, as I found I end up pressing it quite often when defining my curves.

Regarding the name I think auto-tangent is a bit too opaque a name, and I think since it's operating on a totally different node and underlying object (curve3d and curve2d) , I don't see the need to keep it consistent with what is implemented for BezierTrackEditor

I do think 'smooth points' is a bit of a misnomer, how would you feel about having it named 'Smooth Curve' and keep it as a button on the hotbar?

There's no need for it to be a button when it might be pressed multiple times. You can use a shortcut instead. However, considering that other options like CloseCurve and ClearPoints are similarly one-shot options, having it as a button might be “temporarily” acceptable. But in any case, there are too many buttons in CurveEditorTools, so I think it should be organized into a pull-down menu in a later follow-up PR.

“Smooth Curve” is odd since the path is a polygon unless you extend the curve handles, situations arise where you apply it to something that can't be called a curve.

Also, if pressing multiple times provides an effect where the corner radius progressively increases with each press, similar to a blur, then using the term “smoothing” is somewhat appropriate. However, when providing a single deterministic result from the current point, "smoothing" is never a more appropriate term than "Auto Tangent".

Especially the case for users who have already obtained a smooth curve, applying this option could result in overwriting and potentially making it less smooth than before. Therefore, it is better to indicate that this is merely an automatic calculation rather than applying smoothing to the current state.

> There's no need for it to be a button when it might be pressed multiple times. You can use a shortcut instead. However, considering that other options like CloseCurve and ClearPoints are similarly one-shot options, having it as a button might be “temporarily” acceptable. But in any case, there are too many buttons in CurveEditorTools, so I think it should be organized into a pull-down menu in a later follow-up PR.
 
 - Okay that sounds good to me, i'll make it a button for now and maybe we can work together in future to organize things better in this sense
 
> “Smooth Curve” is odd since the path is a polygon unless you extend the curve handles, situations arise where you apply it to something that can't be called a curve.

  - I see what you mean partially, but as soon as you press the button, it stops being a polygon and becomes a smooth curve, which in my view makes a lot of sense from a users perspective  

But I see your point and I'm happy to go with auto-tangent, although I feel it's a bit less intuitive in some cases

With such an implementation, this would match the rejection case for the proposal, where "it would be sufficient as an add-on".

What do you mean by implementing this in the core? Do you mean moving the smoothing function to Path3D rather than the editor? 

> So probably, in addition to the current implementation, which applies to all paths, implementing a toggle option that applies this only to the clicked point as similar to deletion mode would provide the justification for implementing this in the core.

I dont understand what you're trying to say, do you mean you don't think this should be a feature of the editor unless we add the point selection? Im not sure I like the idea of having a different usage patterns between path2d and path3d, I would love to bring them both into cohesion in terms of implementation, but that seems out of scope for this PR

> What do you mean by implementing this in the core? Do you mean moving the smoothing function to Path3D rather than the editor?

For example, in Delete mode, after toggling the Delete button on, only the clicked point is deleted. Similarly, it should be possible to set auto tangent only for the clicked point.

Although this is a remnant behavior from when there was no selection function (in Path3D), but it allows you to edit the path while focusing on a single point even if it in Path2DEditor.

Since focusing on a single point requires using an API not exposed from the core, this implies that there is value in merging this feature into the core rather than leaving it as an add-on.

As I mentioned above, as long as it can't control individual points, making it to be an add-on is sufficient.

Although the sentence was removed from the issue submission template because so few people read it, there is a clear internal standard stating that proposals deemed sufficient as add-ons are invalid.

---

As I’ve said many times, only applying features to the all points is not so practical/matured because it overwrites the existing path. And it can definitely be done using just add-ons without core changes.

Refer to the deletion options (with x icon) and implement that they can be applied to individual points. If not, you will first need to improve the core functionality to allow selection of individual points even in 2D, and then refine this PR based on that PR.

It is true that this could be implemented via addons without core changes. But I think there’s still value in considering QOL and usability improvements in the official editor experience. For example, some basic toolbar actions could technically live in addons, but features like clearing points or closing a curve are essential enough for usability that the editor would feel incomplete without them, I think the same applies for the auto tangent feature.

Regarding applying smoothing to all points: I understand the concern about overwriting existing paths, but I’m not fully convinced this is a limiting factor in practice. 

You mentioned that if someone has already achieved a smooth curve it would erase their work?  

If they have already achieved a smooth curve that they are happy with they would not be using this feature, or they could simply undo that.
 
Could you share a concrete use case where this becomes problematic? 

That would help me better understand the scenario you're optimizing for.

From my perspective, there are a few common workflows when using Path3D editor:

- Carefully placing control points for precise shapes  -> Supported by manually editing control points

- Generating a reasonable/smooth path where exact control placement isn’t critical -> Now supported by auto tangent button

- Using generated paths as a starting point for further manual refinement -> Now supported by auto tangent button

I’ve also noticed that new suggestions have been coming in incrementally across revisions. It might help to consolidate them where possible so we can evaluate the overall direction more effectively and reduce iteration overhead.

Overall, I think the initial feature already provides solid value, the Spinbox in my view is a nice to have but I don't particularly like the look/ feel of exposing it on the toolbar, the addition proposed of individually selecting points to smooth, seem to be overcomplicating it without a clear usecase in mind.

If you disagree, do you mind clearly elaborating your position so I can understand where you are coming from?

> Could you share a concrete use case where this becomes problematic? To give a specific example, consider a case like rounding the corners of the paths that make up a glyph. Since glyphs already contain curves, we need to avoid distorting those curves. This might not be an issue if you smooth the entire object first before creating the text, but you cannot apply this to existing projects or to paths imported from plugins or other sources. > If you disagree, do you mind clearly elaborating your position so I can understand where you are coming from? First and foremost, there is a philosophy that features which can be adequately implemented via add-ons should not be added to the core unnecessarily. This stems from [Best practices for engine contributors](https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/engine/guidelines/best_practices.html#cater-to-common-use-cases-leave-the-door-open-for-the-rare-ones). In fact, this is why several PRs have been blocked in the past and ended up as add-ons or custom modules. As I recall, this occurred with PRs for import plugins, among others. The template for the old Proposal repository included a question asking whether an add-on would suffice, and there was an obligation to answer it. ``` Is there a reason why this should be core and not an add-on in the asset library?* ``` That text was removed with the intention of reusing the proposal repository as a place to propose add-on ideas. We are currently in a transitional phase of organizing these documents, and it was unfortunate for you that this wasn’t clear. We are in the process of adding text to clarify this. See also https://github.com/godotengine/godot-contributing-docs/pull/81. I understand the demand for this feature to some extent, but as I mentioned earlier, it doesn’t address cases where we want to avoid overwriting, so personally, I don’t consider it sufficiently practical. We have confirmed time and again that as long as the core features are not fully utilized, meaning the internal API is not being used, an add-on is sufficient. Furthermore, there are several possible approaches to configuring the curve (like https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/14248#issuecomment-3911237278). In such cases, rather than having to merge changes into the master branch every time a user wants to customize smoothing method, an add-on allows users to perform updates more frequently.

I think this does make sense as a core feature. It's an enhancement for an existing editor; since the curve editor can't be extended, it could be cumbersome to use if implemented as an addon. Also the code changes are relatively small.

Smoothing individual points can be implemented later (assuming it won't require completely replacing the current implementation).

> since the curve editor can't be extended, it could be cumbersome to use if implemented as an addon.

@KoBeWi While I respect your opinion in favor of this feature, but it is clearly incorrect.

This PR does not currently use the internal API, and since add-ons can place buttons at the top of the viewport, it is entirely possible to create an add-on that functions exactly like this PR including undo and redo.

I've tested this PR briefly and I tend to agree that it should be possible to smooth selected points only. Until then, it might not be a good idea to merge, as people might not realize their entire path is being modified when clicking the button, even if you have some points selected.

From an UX perspective, if you have some points selected, you'd logically expect only these points to be affected, and the rest of the path should remain unchanged.

> From an UX perspective, if you have some points selected, you'd logically expect only these points to be affected, and the rest of the path should remain unchanged.

We have implemented an undo capability so people can adress unintended editing.

What are the continuity and geometric continuity promises we want to make?

> What are the continuity and geometric continuity promises we want to make?

The algorithm enforces G1 continuity, it explicitly aligns the tangent directions across the selected joint, giving you a smooth visual transition without a kink.

We wouldn't want to use anything beyond that. Higher order continuity would sacrifice control for the user, i.e. G2, C1, C2  would remove most of the degrees of freedom from the curve which is counterproductive when trying to achieving a desired curve.

Do I understand correctly that to convert points back to sharp I need to set the slider to `0` and then click the Apply Auto Tangent button? I think there needs to be a button to set them to zero in one click because that's the usual UX in most vector editors: The slider itself is missing a tooltip so it may not be very obvious what it controls:
I'm not sure why Auto Tangent needs to also be a mode, wouldn't buttons to convert selected be enough? Is the slider important enough to always be on screen? Space is kinda valuable there So the direction I'd suggest taking this in is: - Repurpose the current Auto Tangent mode as convert button, add "convert to linear" alongside it, make sure they are separated from the mode buttons with a separator - Move the slider from the top bar into the settings popup where it can get an explicit Label. You'd need to change it from a popup menu into a popup panel While we're at it maybe we could also change the options button to an icon button: It looks like the path editor overall could use more work in terms of UX, but those are the thoughts directly relevant to this PR

Hello! Just to flag that I started a discussion on making Path3D UI/tools more consistent with Path2D UI/tools a while back here:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/12485

This conversation can help defining what we want to take from Path2D, and what we want to take from Path3D and decide on a better, more consistent design.

> It looks like the path editor overall could use more work in terms of UX, but those are the thoughts directly relevant to this PR

I do agree the UX is not really ideal, but it would be a shame to gate this feature, which I think is still useful and popular untill we can figure out what to do to path2d and path3d.

I am happy to see a new discussion around this topic and I would love to help contribute to improving the UX in the future, some of your comments are things that I cannot apply at the moment, for instance it does not seem to be possible to add tooltips to an editor_spin_slider.  Maybe another thing to work on.


Anyway, I have agreed to work on follow up PRs to iterate on code refactors and usability
